docs.text: Identity Intelligence Platform

docs.title: OSINT-D2
docs.text:
Turn a username into a structured identity dossier. Not a Sherlock wrapper — an autonomous AI agent that reasons, pivots, and cross-correlates across 30+ platforms.

Quick Start Source Code

30+ Platform Scanners 9 Agent Tools 6D Cognitive Profile 5 Languages

docs.title: Why OSINT-D2?
docs.text:
Most OSINT tools run a fixed checklist: scan this list of sites, check this API, generate a report. OSINT-D2 is different — it thinks.

The core of the platform is an agentic AI that uses LLM function calling to autonomously investigate identities. It starts with what you give it (a username, an email), scans it, analyzes the results, and pivots — discovering new leads and investigating them without being told to.

A real investigation: the agent scanned torvalds, found the GitHub profile, extracted two email addresses, scanned both as separate identities, fetched the GitHub and Keybase pages for social links, and identified that multiple people share the handle across platforms — producing a report that distinguishes the real Linus Torvalds from impersonators.

docs.title: Agentic AI
docs.text: The LLM decides which tools to invoke, interprets results, and pivots to new leads. ReAct reasoning loop with forced-report fallback when steps are exhausted.

docs.title: Identity Triangulation
docs.text: Cross-correlates usernames, emails, bios, avatars, and writing style across platforms. Perceptual avatar hashing (dHash) detects the same photo even when resized.

docs.title: 6D Cognitive Profiling
docs.text: Every investigation produces a structured analysis across 6 dimensions: Identity, Geo-temporal, OCEAN Psychology, Tech Stack, Ideology, and OpSec/Attack Surface.

docs.title: Trust Anchor Verification
docs.text: Declare known-good sources (--trust github:user). The system builds a reference identity and uses 4-signal weighted scoring (name, bio, avatar, location) to filter false positives.

docs.title: Classified-Style PDF Dossiers
docs.text: Generate intelligence briefs with identity cards, OCEAN profiles, risk matrices, and entity graphs. CSS-rendered via WeasyPrint with Playwright fallback.

docs.title: 5 Languages, Full Stack
docs.text: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Russian — across CLI, web dashboard, AI prompts, and PDF reports. Not just translated labels; the AI system prompt changes per language.

docs.title: See It In Action
docs.text: Agent Mode — autonomous investigation with real-time reasoning Trust anchors verified 1 source and discarded 2 false positives 6D cognitive profile — identity, geo-temporal, psychological analysis

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git && cd osint-d2
cp .env.example .env          # Add your API keys
docker compose up -d           # Dashboard at http://localhost:8000

Or investigate from the command line:

# Quick scan across 18+ platforms
osint-d2 scan johndoe

# Autonomous AI agent with 10 reasoning steps
osint-d2 agent johndoe --ai-provider deepseek --max-steps 10

# Full pipeline with Sherlock (400+ sites) + breach check
osint-d2 hunt -u johndoe,jdoe123 -e john@example.com --sherlock --breach-check

Full Installation Guide Agent Mode Deep Dive

docs.title: v3.0.0 (2026-10-17)
docs.text: Major infrastructure hardening release for production deployment.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• CORS lockdown — dashboard no longer uses allow_origins=["*"]; restricted to localhost with OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS override for LAN access
  • CDN elimination — all frontend dependencies (vis-network, Font Awesome, DOMPurify) vendorized for offline operation and supply-chain safety
  • XSS defense — SVG and report highlights sanitized with DOMPurify
  • Non-root Docker — container runs as unprivileged osint user

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
• Fixed container startup — removed --no-root from Poetry install that prevented the package from loading
  • Playwright cache — properly copied to non-root user with cleanup (~400 MB savings)
  • Healthcheck — replaced curl dependency with Python urllib
  • Smoke test — CI now verifies container starts before publishing

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
• PyInstaller — collect_all("weasyprint") ensures PDF generation works in standalone binaries
  • PyPI metadata — classifiers, homepage, and documentation URLs added to pyproject.toml

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Fixed incorrect pip install osint-d2 reference in Windows installation guide
  • Added OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS to configuration reference
  • Documented Docker security model (non-root, zero-CDN, batteries-included)

docs.title: REST API Endpoints
docs.text: The OSINT-D2 web server exposes a REST API for programmatic access.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: http://localhost:8000

docs.title: GET / — Dashboard
docs.text:
Returns the HTML dashboard page.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description lang string UI language: en, es, pt, ar, ru (default: en)

docs.title: POST /api/investigate — Start Investigation
docs.text:
Launches an asynchronous investigation. Results are streamed via WebSocket.

Request Body (JSON):

{
  "target": "John Doe",
  "usernames": ["johndoe", "jdoe123"],
  "emails": ["john@example.com"],
  "phones": ["+1 555 123 4567"],
  "trust_anchors": ["github:johndoe"],
  "mode": "agent",
  "ai_provider": "deepseek",
  "language": "en",
  "max_steps": 10,
  "enable_breach_check": false
}

Response:

{
  "investigation_id": "a1b2c3d4",
  "status": "started",
  "target": "John Doe"
}

Modes:

Mode Description agent Autonomous AI investigation with function calling hunt Full OSINT pipeline without AI reasoning phone Telecom-only investigation

docs.title: POST /api/cancel/{inv_id} — Cancel Investigation
docs.text:
Stops a running investigation.

Response:

{
  "status": "cancelled",
  "investigation_id": "a1b2c3d4"
}

docs.title: GET /api/download/{inv_id}/{file_type} — Download Artifacts
docs.text:
Downloads generated artifacts from a completed investigation.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Values Description file_type pdf Classified-style PDF dossier file_type canvas Obsidian Canvas file (.canvas) file_type json Raw investigation data (JSON) file_type graph_html Interactive HTML entity graph

Response Headers:

File Type Content-Type pdf application/pdf canvas application/json json application/json graph_html text/html

Error (404):

{
  "detail": "PDF not generated yet."
}

File generation

PDF and HTML graph files are generated asynchronously during investigation. They may not be available immediately after the investigation completes — wait a few seconds for the rendering pipeline (WeasyPrint/Playwright) to finish.

| running | Investigation in progress | | completed | All scanners finished | | cancelled | User-cancelled | | error | Failed with error |

No dedicated status endpoint

Investigation status is delivered in real-time via WebSocket messages (type: "status"). There is no GET /api/status/{inv_id} endpoint — connect to the WebSocket to receive status updates.

docs.title: WebSocket Protocol
docs.text: OSINT-D2 streams investigation results in real-time via WebSocket.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
ws://localhost:8000/ws/{investigation_id}

Connect after receiving the investigation_id from POST /api/investigate.

docs.title: Message Format
docs.text:
All messages are JSON with a type field and a data field:

{
  "type": "<message_type>",
  "data": "<payload>"
}

docs.title: Example Client
docs.text:
const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://localhost:8000/ws/${investigationId}`);

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);

  switch (msg.type) {
    case 'log':
      console.log(msg.data);
      break;
    case 'node_add':
      graph.addNode(msg.data);
      break;
    case 'report_done':
      showReport(msg.data);
      break;
    case 'status':
      if (msg.data === 'completed') ws.close();
      break;
  }
};

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 follows Clean Architecture with strict separation between domain logic and I/O adapters. The codebase is organized into three layers.

graph TB
    subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"]
        M["cli/main.py<br/>Typer + Rich"]
        D["cli/doctor.py"]
    end

    subgraph Core["Core (Domain + Services)"]
        Config["config.py<br/>AppSettings (Pydantic)"]
        Models["domain/models.py<br/>PersonEntity, SocialProfile, AnalysisReport"]
        Pipeline["services/identity_pipeline.py<br/>Scan orchestration"]
        Agent["services/agent_engine.py<br/>ReAct reasoning loop"]
        Tools["services/agent_tools.py<br/>9 tool definitions + dispatcher"]
        Trust["services/trust_anchor.py<br/>4-signal verification"]
        Guard["services/url_guard.py<br/>SSRF protection"]
    end

    subgraph Adapters["Adapters (I/O)"]
        HTTP["http_client.py<br/>httpx + proxy support"]
        VS["vector_store.py<br/>BM25 + stylometry"]
        Scanners["osint_sources/<br/>20 platform scanners"]
        Breach["breach_check.py<br/>HaveIBeenPwned"]
        Avatar["avatar_analyzer.py<br/>Perceptual dHash"]
        Phone["phone_scanner.py<br/>E.164 + carrier lookup"]
        Report["report_exporter.py<br/>PDF/HTML generation"]
        Graph["graph_exporter.py<br/>Entity graphs"]
        Web["web_server.py<br/>FastAPI + WebSocket"]
        Rate["rate_limiter.py<br/>Per-domain throttle"]
    end

    M --> Pipeline
    M --> Agent
    Web --> Pipeline
    Web --> Agent
    Agent --> Tools
    Tools --> Pipeline
    Tools --> VS
    Tools --> Avatar
    Tools --> Phone
    Tools --> Breach
    Tools --> HTTP
    Tools --> Guard
    Pipeline --> Scanners
    Pipeline --> Trust
    Scanners --> HTTP
    HTTP --> Rate

    style Core fill:#0a1a14,stroke:#2dd4bf,color:#fff
    style Adapters fill:#111b22,stroke:#1a9a87,color:#c9d1d9
    style CLI fill:#0d1117,stroke:#8b949e,color:#c9d1d9

docs.title: Core
docs.text: The core contains zero I/O — no HTTP calls, no filesystem access, no database queries. All I/O is delegated to adapters.

docs.title: Domain Models (core/domain/models.py)
docs.text:
Three Pydantic v2 models define the investigation data:

Model Purpose PersonEntity Root aggregate: target identifier + discovered profiles + optional AI analysis SocialProfile One profile on one platform: URL, username, network, exists flag, bio, avatar, metadata dict AnalysisReport AI-generated analysis: summary, highlights, confidence score, model used, raw payload

Additional models: HaveibeenpwnedBreach, HaveibeenpwnedProfiles for breach data.

docs.title: Agent Engine (core/services/agent_engine.py)
docs.text:
The ReAct reasoning loop. See Agent Mode for details.

Key decisions: - Uses the OpenAI client (compatible with DeepSeek, Ollama, Groq, any OpenAI-compatible API) - Forced report fallback: if the agent exhausts steps, forces generate_report with tool_choice - Profile collection: every tool result is parsed for SocialProfile-like entries and indexed into the vector store - Explicit target: the target identifier is set by the caller (CLI/web), never guessed from the free-text objective

docs.title: Trust Anchor Verification (core/services/trust_anchor.py)
docs.text: 4-signal weighted identity verification. See Trust Anchor System for the full deep-dive.

docs.title: URL Guard (core/services/url_guard.py)
docs.text: SSRF protection for the fetch_url agent tool. Blocks requests to: - Private IP ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x, 192.168.x.x) - Loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost) - Link-local (169.254.x.x) - Cloud IMDS endpoints (169.254.169.254)

docs.title: Platform Scanners (adapters/osint_sources/)
docs.text:
20 dedicated scanners, each implementing platform-specific extraction:

Scanner Method Extracted data GitHub REST API Name, bio, location, email, repos, blog, Twitter link GitLab REST API Name, bio, avatar Instagram Web scraping + OG tags Name, bio, followers, avatar Facebook mbasic.facebook.com Name, location, education X (Twitter) Web scraping Bio, followers, avatar Telegram t.me Display name, bio, avatar Reddit JSON API Karma, cake day, bio Medium REST API Name, bio, avatar Pinterest Web scraping Name, bio, boards count Twitch GQL API Display name, bio, avatar + 10 more Various Platform-specific metadata

Additionally, data-driven site lists (WhatsMyName format) extend coverage to hundreds of additional sites without dedicated scrapers.

docs.title: Vector Store (adapters/vector_store.py)
docs.text:
Pure-Python in-memory search engine with two capabilities:

  1. Semantic search (BM25): retrieve previously collected evidence by concept
  2. Stylometric correlation: compare writing styles using character n-gram cosine similarity

Technical details: - No heavy deps: no numpy, scipy, or ML frameworks. Sparse dicts + math only. - Trilingual stemming: light suffix stripping for Spanish, English, Portuguese - Accent folding: Unicode NFD normalization strips diacritics - BM25 parameters: k1=1.5 (term frequency saturation), b=0.75 (document length normalization) - Stylometry guard: minimum 40 characters to prevent false certainty from short texts

docs.title: Rate Limiter (adapters/rate_limiter.py)
docs.text:
Responsible scanning with per-domain throttling:

Setting Default Env Var Delay between requests 200ms OSINT_D2_REQUEST_DELAY_MS Jitter ±100ms OSINT_D2_REQUEST_JITTER_MS Per-domain concurrency 3 OSINT_D2_PER_DOMAIN_CONCURRENCY Retry attempts (429/503) 3 OSINT_D2_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS Global concurrency 30 OSINT_D2_SITES_MAX_CONCURRENCY

Exponential backoff with jitter on 429/503 responses.

docs.title: Report Exporter (adapters/report_exporter.py)
docs.text:
Generates classified-style PDF dossiers with: - Identity card with avatar, classification level, and evidence tags - 6D cognitive profile sections - Entity relationship graph - Risk/confidence matrix - Full evidence appendix

Rendering pipeline: Jinja2 HTML template → WeasyPrint CSS rendering → PDF. Falls back to Playwright (headless Chromium) if WeasyPrint fails.

docs.title: Avatar Analyzer (adapters/avatar_analyzer.py)
docs.text:
Perceptual image comparison using difference hash (dHash): 1. Resize to 9x8 grayscale 2. Compare adjacent pixels to generate 64-bit hash 3. Hamming distance between hashes = dissimilarity

Robust to JPEG compression, resizing, and minor color adjustments. Used by the agent's compare_avatars tool.

docs.title: HTTP Client (adapters/http_client.py)
docs.text: Centralized httpx.AsyncClient factory with: - Configurable proxy support (ScrapingAnt residential/datacenter) - Custom User-Agent - Timeout management - HTML metadata extraction (title, description, social links, emails in page)

docs.title: Configuration (core/config.py)
docs.text:
All configuration via pydantic-settings with the OSINT_D2_ prefix:

  • Resolution order: env vars → project .env → user ~/.config/osint-d2/.env
  • Cross-platform: Windows (%APPDATA%), macOS (~/Library/Application Support), Linux (~/.config)
  • Typed validation: Pydantic enforces types, ranges, and constraints at startup

docs.title: Trust Anchor System
docs.text:
OSINT-D2's Trust Anchor system solves a fundamental problem in OSINT: false positives. When you scan the username chad across 30+ platforms, multiple different people share that handle. Trust anchors let you declare which profiles are known to belong to your target, and the system automatically filters the rest.

The problem

Scanning torvalds finds profiles on GitHub (Linus Torvalds), Pinterest (Marco Migozzi), Kaggle (Pengze Lin), and Telegram (unknown). Without trust anchors, the agent might conflate all of them into one person.

docs.title: 1. Declare Anchors
docs.text:
Pass known-good identifiers with the --trust flag:

osint-d2 agent torvalds --trust github:torvalds --trust email:torvalds@linux-foundation.org

Supported anchor types:

Type Format Example Network network:username github:torvalds, instagram:xkissmely Email email:address email:john@example.com

Multiple anchors can be combined. Their signals are merged into a single reference identity.

docs.title: 2. Build Reference Identity
docs.text:
The system scans trusted profiles first and extracts identity signals:

TrustAnchor("github", "torvalds")
    → Scan github.com/torvalds
    → Extract: name="Linus Torvalds", location="Portland, OR"
    → Extract: bio keywords = ["linux", "kernel", "git"]
    → Extract: avatar hash = md5(avatar_url)[:12]

TrustAnchor("email", "torvalds@linux-foundation.org")
    → Split email: "torvalds" (already known from username)
    → Add to reference emails

Email anchors use a heuristic name splitter that can decompose concatenated addresses:

Email Extracted Name kissmely.marcano@gmail.com kissmely marcano john_doe@gmail.com john doe kissmelymarcano@gmail.com kissmely marcano (with username hint xkissmely)

When known usernames are provided (from non-email anchors), the splitter uses them as hints. For example, knowing the username xkissmely helps split kissmelymarcano into kissmely + marcano by finding the username substring within the email.

docs.title: 3. Verify Profiles
docs.text:
After scanning all networks, each discovered profile is compared against the reference using 4-signal weighted scoring:

Signal Weight What it checks Name 40% Display name vs reference names. Exact match = 40pts. Partial overlap = 20-40pts. Bio keywords 30% Keyword overlap between profile bio and trusted bios. 50%+ overlap = full score. Avatar 20% MD5 hash of image URL matches any reference avatar hash. Location 10% Substring match against reference locations.

Confidence threshold: profiles below 30% confidence are flagged as false positives.

docs.title: 4. Name Contradiction Detection
docs.text:
The most powerful signal is name contradiction. If the reference identity establishes the target as "Kissmely Marcano" and a profile shows "Kissmely Almonte", the different surname triggers a hard contradiction — the profile is almost certainly a different person.

Reference names: {"kissmely marcano"}
Profile name:    "kissmely almonte"
    → Overlap: {"kissmely"} ✓
    → Contradiction: {"almonte"} ✗ (not in any reference name)
    → Hard contradiction (len("almonte") >= 4) → score = 0
    → Verdict: FALSE POSITIVE

This prevents the agent from merging different people who happen to share a first name or common handle.

docs.title: Visual Example
docs.text:
Trust anchors discarded 2 false positive(s) from a scan of "torvalds"

The screenshot shows a scan where github:torvalds was declared as a trust anchor. After scanning 18+ platforms, the system verified each profile against the reference built from GitHub and automatically discarded profiles belonging to different people.

docs.title: In Agent Mode
docs.text:
When trust anchors are provided to Agent Mode, the system prompt is augmented with a TRUSTED SOURCES block:

TRUSTED SOURCES (user-verified data):
- VERIFIED GITHUB account: @torvalds
- VERIFIED EMAIL: torvalds@linux-foundation.org

IMPORTANT: Use these as ground truth. If a profile on another
network has a different name/surname than what these sources
suggest, that profile likely belongs to a DIFFERENT PERSON.
Do NOT conflate identities.

This context is injected into the LLM's conversation, ensuring the AI agent respects the ground truth throughout its investigation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Trust anchors work in all modes:

# Agent mode
osint-d2 agent target --trust github:user --trust email:user@domain.com

# Interactive CLI (prompted)
osint-d2
# → "Add trusted identity sources?" [y/n]: y
# → Trust anchor(s) (): github:torvalds

# Web dashboard
# → Configure trust anchors in the sidebar before starting

Best practice

Start with the platform where you're most confident about the target's identity. GitHub profiles with real names and locations make excellent anchors because they provide all 4 signals (name, bio, avatar, location).

docs.title: Adding a Scanner
docs.text: Step-by-step guide to adding a new OSINT data source to OSINT-D2.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: OSINT-D2 scanners follow Clean Architecture: each scanner is an adapter that implements the OSINTScanner protocol. The core pipeline discovers and invokes scanners automatically.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Scanner
docs.text:
Create a new file in src/adapters/osint_sources/:

# src/adapters/osint_sources/newplatform.py
"""NewPlatform scanner — discovers user profiles via their public API."""

from __future__ import annotations

import httpx

from core.domain.models import SocialProfile
from core.interfaces.scanner import OSINTScanner


class NewPlatformScanner(OSINTScanner):
    """Scans NewPlatform for a username."""

    PLATFORM = "newplatform"

    async def scan_username(
        self,
        username: str,
        client: httpx.AsyncClient,
    ) -> SocialProfile | None:
        """Check if the username exists on NewPlatform."""
        url = f"https://api.newplatform.com/users/{username}"

        try:
            resp = await client.get(url)
            if resp.status_code == 404:
                return SocialProfile(
                    url=url,
                    username=username,
                    network_name=self.PLATFORM,
                    exists=False,
                )

            data = resp.json()
            return SocialProfile(
                url=f"https://newplatform.com/{username}",
                username=username,
                network_name=self.PLATFORM,
                exists=True,
                bio=data.get("bio"),
                image_url=data.get("avatar_url"),
                metadata={
                    "source": "newplatform_api",
                    "followers": data.get("followers_count"),
                    "created_at": data.get("created_at"),
                },
            )
        except Exception:
            return None

docs.title: Step 2: Implement the Protocol
docs.text:
Your scanner must match the OSINTScanner protocol defined in src/core/interfaces/scanner.py:

class OSINTScanner(Protocol):
    PLATFORM: str

    async def scan_username(
        self,
        username: str,
        client: httpx.AsyncClient,
    ) -> SocialProfile | None: ...

Key rules:

  • Return SocialProfile(exists=True, ...) when the profile is found
  • Return SocialProfile(exists=False, ...) when confirmed not found
  • Return None on network errors (the pipeline handles retries)
  • Never raise exceptions — catch and return None

docs.title: Step 3: Register in the Pipeline
docs.text:
Add your scanner to src/core/services/identity_pipeline.py:

from adapters.osint_sources.newplatform import NewPlatformScanner

_USERNAME_SCANNERS = (
    # ... existing scanners ...
    NewPlatformScanner,
)

docs.title: Step 4: Add a Test
docs.text:
Create tests/test_newplatform_scanner.py:

import pytest
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock

from adapters.osint_sources.newplatform import NewPlatformScanner


class TestNewPlatformScanner:
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_found_profile(self):
        scanner = NewPlatformScanner()
        mock_resp = MagicMock()
        mock_resp.status_code = 200
        mock_resp.json.return_value = {
            "bio": "Developer",
            "followers_count": 100,
        }

        client = AsyncMock()
        client.get.return_value = mock_resp

        result = await scanner.scan_username("testuser", client)
        assert result is not None
        assert result.exists is True
        assert result.network_name == "newplatform"

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_not_found(self):
        scanner = NewPlatformScanner()
        mock_resp = MagicMock()
        mock_resp.status_code = 404

        client = AsyncMock()
        client.get.return_value = mock_resp

        result = await scanner.scan_username("nonexistent", client)
        assert result is not None
        assert result.exists is False

docs.title: Step 5: Verify
docs.text:
# Run your test
poetry run pytest tests/test_newplatform_scanner.py -v

# Run the full suite
poetry run pytest tests/ -v

# Lint
poetry run ruff check src/adapters/osint_sources/newplatform.py

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use the metadata dict for platform-specific data (followers, repos, karma, etc.)
  • Populate bio when available — the AI uses it for cognitive profiling
  • Set image_url for the PDF dossier identity card
  • Check HIGH_SIGNAL_PLATFORMS in graph_exporter.py — add your platform if it provides meaningful intelligence signals

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text: Complete guide for setting up an OSINT-D2 development environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+ (3.12 recommended)
  • Poetry (dependency management)
  • Git

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2

# Install all dependencies (including dev extras)
poetry install

# Install Playwright browser for PDF generation
playwright install chromium

# Copy environment template
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your API keys (optional for development)

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 is configured via environment variables. Create a .env file from the template:

cp .env.example .env

Or use the interactive setup:

osint-d2 doctor setup-ai

docs.title: AI Provider
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY — API key for the AI provider. Required for AI analysis and agent mode. Supports DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible API. OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL https://api.deepseek.com Base URL for the AI API. Change for Ollama (http://localhost:11434/v1) or other providers. OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL deepseek-chat Model name to use for analysis. OSINT_D2_AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 45 Timeout in seconds for AI API calls. OSINT_D2_AI_MAX_RETRIES 3 Max retries on transient AI failures (rate limits, network errors).

docs.title: Proxy (ScrapingAnt)
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_PROXY_API_KEY — ScrapingAnt API key. Enables proxy routing for all scanner requests. OSINT_D2_PROXY_USERNAME — ScrapingAnt username for standalone proxy products. OSINT_D2_PROXY_MODE residential Proxy type: residential (recommended) or datacenter. OSINT_D2_PROXY_COUNTRY — 2-letter country code for geo-targeting (e.g., us, de, br).

docs.title: HTTP & Rate Limiting
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 20 Timeout per HTTP request in seconds. OSINT_D2_USER_AGENT osint-d2/3.0 User-Agent header for OSINT requests. OSINT_D2_SITES_MAX_CONCURRENCY 30 Max concurrent requests across all site-list scanners. OSINT_D2_REQUEST_DELAY_MS 200 Minimum delay (ms) between requests to the same domain. OSINT_D2_REQUEST_JITTER_MS 100 Random jitter ± (ms) added to delay for naturalness. OSINT_D2_PER_DOMAIN_CONCURRENCY 3 Max simultaneous requests to the same domain. OSINT_D2_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Retries on 429/503 responses with exponential backoff.

docs.title: Language & Scanning
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE en Default language for CLI prompts, AI analysis, and PDF reports. Options: en, es, pt, ar, ru. OSINT_D2_SITES_NO_NSFW true Exclude NSFW categories from site-list scans. OSINT_D2_USERNAME_SITES_PATH — Path to custom username sites JSON (WhatsMyName format). OSINT_D2_EMAIL_SITES_PATH — Path to custom email sites JSON.

docs.title: Web Server
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS http://localhost:8000,http://127.0.0.1:8000 Comma-separated list of allowed CORS origins. Set this to access the dashboard from LAN hosts.

docs.title: Agent Mode
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_AGENT_MAX_STEPS 10 Maximum reasoning steps for autonomous agent investigations.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+ (tested on 3.11, 3.12, 3.13)
  • Poetry for dependency management
  • Playwright Chromium — required for graph PNG rendering (manual install: playwright install chromium)

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Poetry (recommended)pipDockerStandalone Binary (PyInstaller) 
git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2
poetry install
poetry run playwright install chromium

git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2
pip install -e .
playwright install chromium

git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d

Batteries included

The Docker image includes all native dependencies (Cairo, Pango, Chromium). No additional system setup needed — PDFs, graph PNGs, and the web dashboard work out of the box.

See the Docker Deployment guide for full configuration.

git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2
poetry install
pyinstaller -y packaging/pyinstaller/osint-d2.spec

The binary is output to dist/osint-d2/. After building:

# Required for graph PNG rendering:
playwright install chromium

# Required for PDF generation (system packages):
# Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install libcairo2 libpango-1.0-0 libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0
# macOS:  brew install cairo pango gdk-pixbuf

Native dependencies

The standalone binary bundles Python code but not native system libraries. PDF generation requires Cairo/Pango on the host, and graph PNG rendering requires a Chromium install via Playwright.

docs.title: System Dependencies
docs.text:
Playwright and WeasyPrint require native libraries for headless browser rendering and PDF generation.

Ubuntu / DebianFedora / RHELmacOSWindows 
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y \
    libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 \
    libpango-1.0-0 \
    libpangocairo-1.0-0 \
    libcairo2 \
    libffi-dev \
    shared-mime-info

Debian Trixie / bookworm

The package is libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 (with hyphens), not libgdk-pixbuf2.0-0 (without hyphens). The latter was deprecated in recent Debian versions.

sudo dnf install -y \
    gdk-pixbuf2 \
    pango \
    cairo

brew install cairo pango gdk-pixbuf libffi

Install GTK3 runtime for WeasyPrint PDF support, then:

git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2
pip install -e .
playwright install chromium

PyPI

Once published, you'll also be able to install with pip install osint-d2.

docs.title: AI Provider Setup
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 requires an LLM provider for Agent Mode and AI analysis. Choose one:

DeepSeek (default, cheapest)OpenAIOllama (fully offline)
  1. Get an API key at platform.deepseek.com
  2. Configure:
OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com
OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=deepseek-chat

OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=openai
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini
  1. Install Ollama
  2. Pull a model: ollama pull llama3.1
  3. Configure:
OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=ollama
OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=llama3.1

No API key needed — everything runs locally.

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Run the built-in diagnostic tool:

poetry run osint-d2 doctor run

This checks:

  • AI provider configuration (key, base URL, model)
  • HTTP connectivity (outbound request to GitHub)
  • WeasyPrint PDF rendering capability
  • Proxy configuration (ScrapingAnt mode, key, country)

What doctor run does NOT check

It does not verify Python version, installed packages, or Playwright browser availability. To verify Playwright, run playwright install chromium and check for errors.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 reads configuration from two locations (in priority order):

  1. Project .env — in the repository root (development)
  2. User config — ~/.config/osint-d2/.env (cross-platform, PyInstaller-compatible)

All variables use the OSINT_D2_ prefix. See the Configuration reference for the full list.

docs.title: Sherlock (400+ Sites)
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 includes a built-in async Sherlock engine — no external packages required.

When you pass --sherlock to the hunt command, OSINT-D2 automatically downloads the official Sherlock site manifest (data.json) from GitHub and runs checks across 400+ sites using its own concurrent runner.

osint-d2 hunt -u johndoe --sherlock

No pip install sherlock-project needed

Unlike earlier versions, OSINT-D2 v3.0 does not depend on the sherlock-project pip package. The manifest is fetched on demand and cached locally in data/.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide walks you through your first OSINT investigation. In 5 minutes you'll go from a username to a structured intelligence dossier.

poetry run osint-d2

You'll see the OSINT-D2 banner and a guided wizard:

Interactive CLI — the wizard guides you through investigation options

docs.title: 2. Choose an investigation mode
docs.text: Mode What it does Speed Depth username Scan a username across 18+ native scanners ~15s Surface-level profiles email Scan email via Gravatar, PGP keyservers + optional local-part pivot ~20s Email-linked accounts both Combined username + email scan ~30s Broader coverage agent Autonomous AI agent that reasons, pivots, and cross-correlates ~2-5min Deep — 6D cognitive profile

After scanning, OSINT-D2 displays:

Scan results with trust anchor verification filtering false positives

For scripting or quick lookups, use direct CLI commands:

# Full autonomous investigation

docs.title: Agent Mode
docs.text:
OSINT-D2's Agent Mode is the core differentiator: an autonomous AI investigator that uses LLM function calling to reason about evidence, decide what to scan next, and pivot across identities — just like a human analyst, but faster.

Not a script — an agent

Most OSINT tools run a fixed pipeline. Agent Mode uses a ReAct reasoning loop: the AI observes evidence, thinks about what's missing, calls a tool, and repeats until it has enough to build a cognitive profile.

docs.title: How the ReAct Loop Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["📋 User provides target + usernames/emails"] --> B["🧠 LLM receives context + 9 available tools"]
    B --> C{"LLM decides: call a tool or generate report?"}
    C -->|"Call tool"| D["⚡ Execute tool, append result to conversation"]
    D --> E{"Step limit reached?"}
    E -->|"No"| B
    E -->|"Yes"| F["⚠️ Force generate_report with tool_choice"]
    C -->|"generate_report"| G["📊 6D Cognitive Profile produced"]
    F --> G

Each step, the LLM receives the full conversation history (system prompt + all previous tool calls and results) and decides autonomously what to do next. The engine (agent_engine.py) manages the loop, collects discovered profiles, and indexes them into the in-memory vector store for cross-reference.

docs.title: Forced Report Fallback
docs.text: If the agent exhausts its max_steps without calling generate_report, the engine forces one final LLM call with tool_choice={"type": "function", "function": {"name": "generate_report"}} — guaranteeing every investigation produces a structured output, even if the agent was too eager investigating.

docs.title: The 9-Tool Arsenal
docs.text:
The agent has access to 9 tools, each wrapping an existing OSINT scanner and compacting results to fit the LLM context window.

# Tool What it does Key output 1 scan_username Scan across 18+ platforms (GitHub, X, Instagram, Reddit, Telegram, etc.) Confirmed profiles with bios, avatars, metadata 2 scan_email Pivot from email via Gravatar, PGP keyservers, Ubuntu keyserver. Optionally scans local part as username. Cross-platform profiles, PGP keys 3 breach_check HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity check Breach names, dates, compromised data types 4 fetch_url Extract intelligence from any URL: title, emails, social links, OG metadata Discovered usernames, emails, social links 5 compare_avatars Perceptual hashing (dHash) to compare two avatar images Similarity %, hamming distance 6 scan_phone Telecom intelligence: E.164 validation, carrier, country, WhatsApp status Carrier, line type, timezones, footprint URLs 7 search_vector_memory BM25 search across all evidence collected during the investigation Ranked snippets with relevance scores 8 correlate_stylometry Character n-gram stylometric comparison against known target writing Cosine similarity (0-1) per candidate 9 generate_report Finalize investigation with structured 6D analysis Summary, highlights, confidence score

docs.title: SSRF Protection
docs.text: The fetch_url tool validates URLs against private IP ranges and cloud IMDS endpoints before fetching. Attempts to access 169.254.169.254, localhost, 10.x.x.x, or similar are blocked with an SSRFBlockedError.

docs.title: Score Interpretation
docs.text:
Critical — do not misread these

The agent's system prompt explicitly instructs the LLM how to interpret each scoring metric. Misinterpretation leads to false conclusions in the final report.

docs.title: search_vector_memory → BM25 Score
docs.text:
Range Meaning 0 – 1 Weak match — few overlapping terms 1 – 3 Moderate match — relevant content 3 – 5+ Strong match — highly relevant

BM25 scores are not percentages. They depend on corpus size, document length, and term frequency saturation (k1=1.5, b=0.75). A score of 4.2 means "very relevant", not "42%".

docs.title: correlate_stylometry → Cosine Similarity
docs.text:
Range Interpretation > 0.70 Very likely the same author 0.40 – 0.70 Moderate signal — needs corroboration < 0.15 Unrelated writing styles

Based on character 4-gram frequency vectors with accent folding (Calderón → Calderon). Minimum 40 characters required — shorter samples are silently skipped to avoid false certainty.

docs.title: compare_avatars → Perceptual Hash
docs.text:
Metric Interpretation hamming_distance = 0 Identical images hamming_distance ≤ 10 Probably the same photo (resized, recompressed) hamming_distance > 20 Different images similarity_percentage 0–100% based on hamming distance

Uses difference hash (dHash) which is robust to JPEG compression, resizing, and minor color adjustments.

docs.title: Vector Memory Architecture
docs.text:
During an investigation, every discovered profile with text content (bios, descriptions, titles) is indexed into an in-memory vector store. This allows the agent to cross-reference evidence later.

Profile discovered → tokenize (accent fold + trilingual stem) → TF-IDF vector
                                                               → character 4-gram stylometric vector
                     → index in BM25 store

The vector store is pure Python (no numpy/scipy dependency):

  • Accent folding: unicodedata.normalize("NFD") strips diacritics so calderón matches calderon
  • Trilingual stemming: Light suffix stripping for Spanish, English, and Portuguese (desarrollo → desarr, developer → develop)
  • Stopword removal: 150+ stopwords across ES/EN/PT
  • BM25 scoring: Length-normalized term frequency with IDF weighting (not cosine similarity, which penalized long documents)

docs.title: System Prompt Strategy
docs.text:
The agent's system prompt is dynamically constructed based on the investigation language. It includes:

  1. Role definition — "expert OSINT investigator and Criminal Profiler"
  2. Method — 5-step investigation methodology (start → gather → analyze → pivot → report)
  3. Rules — step limits, no data fabrication, pattern recognition guidance
  4. Score interpretation — explicit instructions for BM25, stylometry, and avatar metrics
  5. Report structure — must cover the 6 dimensions
  6. Language — response language matches the investigation

The prompt changes per language. In Spanish, the agent receives instructions in Spanish and responds in "español neutro". This isn't just translation — the investigation methodology description adapts to the linguistic context.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: osint-d2 agent johndoe --ai-provider deepseek --max-steps 10

docs.title: Web Dashboard
docs.text: Select AI Agent mode in the sidebar configuration, set the AI provider and max steps, then click Start Investigation.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
OSINT_D2_AGENT_MAX_STEPS=10       # Default max reasoning steps
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-...        # API key (not needed for Ollama)
OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com
OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=deepseek-chat
Provider Base URL Model DeepSeek https://api.deepseek.com deepseek-chat OpenAI https://api.openai.com/v1 gpt-4o-mini Ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 llama3.1 Groq https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 llama-3.1-70b-versatile

docs.title: 6D Cognitive Profile
docs.text:
When the agent finishes, it generates a structured analysis across 6 dimensions:

Dimension What the agent analyzes Identity & Demographics Real name, aliases, handle patterns, estimated age, gender, education level. Cross-references names across platforms to identify impersonators. Geo-temporal Timezone inference, location signals, language patterns, activity hours, sleep routine estimation OCEAN Psychology Big Five personality traits inferred from writing style, content choices, and online behavior patterns Tech Stack Programming languages, frameworks, tools, platforms, contribution patterns, skill level indicators Ideology & Values Interests, causes, community affiliations, political signals, content themes OpSec / Attack Surface Password reuse signals, email exposure, handle consistency, data breach exposure, privacy hygiene

Real agent output — 6D profile for the handle "torvalds"

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• More steps = deeper investigation — 6 for quick scans, 10-15 for thorough investigations
  • Trust anchors filter false positives — --trust github:johndoe tells the agent that GitHub profile is confirmed
  • Ollama works fully offline — no data leaves your machine
  • The agent never fabricates data — every claim traces back to a tool observation
  • Parallel tool calls: some LLMs (GPT-4o) call multiple tools per step, making investigations faster

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: All commands use the osint-d2 entry point. Use osint-d2 <command> --help for full details.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
These options are available across most commands:

Flag Short Description --language -l Output language: en, es, pt, ar, ru --export-json Export results as JSON to reports/ --export-pdf Export a classified-style PDF dossier to reports/ --ai-provider AI provider preset: deepseek, groq, openai, ollama --ai-key AI API key (prefer osint-d2 doctor setup-ai to avoid shell history leaks) --proxy Override proxy mode: residential, datacenter --no-proxy Disable proxy for this run even if configured in .env --proxy-country 2-letter country code for geo-targeted proxy (e.g. us) --format Terminal output format: table (default) or json --trust Trust anchor (repeatable). Format: network:username

docs.text:

osint-d2 scan <target> [OPTIONS]

docs.text:
Autonomous OSINT investigation powered by agentic AI.

osint-d2 agent <objective> [OPTIONS]

Flag Default Description --ai-provider — AI provider preset: deepseek, groq, openai, ollama --max-steps 10 Maximum reasoning steps before the agent concludes (1–50) --breach-check / --no-breach-check --no-breach-check Allow the agent to query HaveIBeenPwned --trust — Trust anchor (repeatable): --trust github:johndoe --language, -l en Output language --export-json / --no-export-json --no-export-json Export JSON to reports/ --export-pdf / --no-export-pdf --no-export-pdf Export PDF dossier --export-canvas / --no-export-canvas --no-export-canvas Export Obsidian Canvas entity graph --export-html-graph / --no-export-html-graph --no-export-html-graph Export interactive HTML graph

AI model

The model is configured via the OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL environment variable or .env file, not via a CLI flag. Use osint-d2 doctor setup-ai for interactive configuration.

docs.text: Subcommand Description run Run baseline diagnostics and show recommended fixes setup-ai Interactive AI setup (stores config in user .env)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Run full diagnostics
osint-d2 doctor run

# Interactive AI provider setup
osint-d2 doctor setup-ai

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
Launch the real-time web dashboard (FastAPI + WebSockets).

osint-d2 serve [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Short Default Description --host -h 127.0.0.1 Host interface to bind to --port -p 8000 Port number --reload — Enable auto-reload for development

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Start dashboard on default port
osint-d2 serve

# Bind to all interfaces (LAN access)
osint-d2 serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000

docs.title: wizard
docs.text:
Step-by-step interactive assistant for newcomers. No arguments required.

osint-d2 wizard

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Doble-2/osint-d2.git
cd osint-d2
cp .env.example .env          # Add your API keys
docker compose up -d

Open http://localhost:8000 to access the web dashboard.

Batteries Included

The Docker image includes all native dependencies for full functionality:

  • PDF generation — WeasyPrint + Cairo/Pango/GDK-Pixbuf pre-installed
  • Graph PNG rendering — Playwright + Chromium pre-installed
  • Web dashboard — all assets vendorized (no external CDN calls)
  • Non-root execution — runs as unprivileged osint user

No additional setup steps required beyond configuring your AI provider.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All OSINT-D2 configuration uses the OSINT_D2_ prefix. Edit your .env file:

docs.title: AI Provider (required — pick one)
docs.text: Variable Description Example OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER Provider name deepseek, openai, ollama OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY API key (not needed for Ollama) sk-xxxxxxxx OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL Provider endpoint https://api.deepseek.com OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL Model to use deepseek-chat

docs.title: Optional Services
docs.text:
Variable Description OSINT_D2_PROXY_API_KEY ScrapingAnt proxy key for anti-bot bypass OSINT_D2_PROXY_USERNAME ScrapingAnt proxy username OSINT_D2_PROXY_MODE residential or datacenter OSINT_D2_PROXY_COUNTRY 2-letter country code (e.g. us)

Wrong variable names

Previous versions of the documentation used DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY — those are wrong. All variables use the OSINT_D2_ prefix.

docs.title: Passing Variables
docs.text:
.env file (recommended)InlineDocker Compose override 
OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com
OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=deepseek-chat

docker compose up -d

docker run -p 8000:8000 \
  -e OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek \
  -e OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxx \
  ghcr.io/doble-2/osint-d2

# docker-compose.override.yml
services:
  osint-d2:
    environment:
      - OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek
      - OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxx

docs.title: LAN / Network Access
docs.text:
By default, the dashboard's CORS policy restricts access to localhost. To access the dashboard from other machines on your network, set OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS:

# Allow access from any host on the LAN
OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.100:8000,http://my-server.local:8000

docs.title: Ollama (Fully Offline)
docs.text:
Run LLM inference locally with zero data leaving your machine:

# docker-compose.override.yml
services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama_data:/root/.ollama

  osint-d2:
    environment:
      - OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=ollama
      - OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434/v1
      - OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=llama3.1
    depends_on:
      - ollama

volumes:
  ollama_data:

After starting, pull the model:

docker exec ollama ollama pull llama3.1

GPU passthrough

For Nvidia GPUs, add deploy.resources.reservations.devices to the Ollama service. See the Ollama Docker docs.

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text:
Reports are stored in /app/reports inside the container. Mount a local directory to persist them:

volumes:
  - ./reports:/app/reports

Volume permissions

The container runs as user osint (UID 1000). Ensure the mounted directory is writable by UID 1000:

mkdir -p ./reports && chmod 777 ./reports
# or, for tighter permissions:
chown 1000:1000 ./reports

docs.title: Pre-built Image
docs.text:
Pull the latest image from GitHub Container Registry:

docker pull ghcr.io/doble-2/osint-d2:latest
docker run --name osint-d2 -p 8000:8000 --env-file .env ghcr.io/doble-2/osint-d2

The image is built for linux/amd64 via GitHub Actions on every push to main.

ARM / Apple Silicon

The pre-built image is linux/amd64. On ARM machines (Apple Silicon, Raspberry Pi), build locally instead: docker compose build.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The container runs as a non-root user (osint) by default. This provides defense-in-depth: even if Chromium has a sandbox escape vulnerability, the attacker lands in an unprivileged context.

The web dashboard makes zero external network requests — all JavaScript, CSS, and font dependencies are vendorized inside the image. Suitable for air-gapped environments.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
The container includes a built-in health check:

docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' osint-d2

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Resource Requirements
docs.text:
Component Minimum Recommended RAM 512 MB 1 GB CPU 1 core 2 cores Disk 2.5 GB (image) 4 GB (image + reports) Ollama (optional) 4 GB RAM 8+ GB RAM, GPU

The main memory consumer is Playwright (used for PDF rendering). If you only use JSON exports, memory usage is much lower.

docs.title: Language Support
docs.text: OSINT-D2 supports 5 languages across the entire stack: CLI interface, web dashboard, AI system prompts, and PDF reports. This is not superficial label translation — the AI agent's reasoning instructions change per language.

docs.title: Supported Languages
docs.text: Code Language CLI Dashboard AI Prompts PDF Reports en English ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ es Spanish ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ pt Portuguese ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ar Arabic ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ru Russian ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: Setting the Language
docs.text:
CLIEnvironmentWeb Dashboard 
osint-d2 hunt -u johndoe --language es

OSINT_D2_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=en

Use the sidebar dropdown or the URL parameter:

http://localhost:8000/?lang=ar

docs.title: How It Works Under the Hood
AI System Prompts
docs.text:
The agent's system prompt is dynamically constructed based on the investigation language. This isn't just translation — the methodology, rules, and score interpretation guides are all written natively for each language.

EnglishSpanish 
You are an expert OSINT investigator and Criminal Profiler.
Your objective is to build a comprehensive profile of the
target person.

METHOD:
1. Start with what you know (provided username/email)
2. Use the tools to gather evidence from multiple sources
3. Analyze results and decide what to investigate next
4. PIVOT: if you find new emails, usernames, aliases...

RESPONSE LANGUAGE: English.

Eres un investigador OSINT experto y Perfilador Criminalista.
Tu objetivo es construir un perfil completo de la persona
indicada.

MÉTODO:
1. Empieza con lo que sabes (username/email proporcionado)
2. Usa las herramientas para recopilar evidencia
3. Analiza los resultados y decide qué investigar después
4. PIVOTEA: si encuentras emails, usernames, aliases...

IDIOMA DE RESPUESTA: Español neutro.

The prompts also include language-specific score interpretation so the LLM doesn't misinterpret BM25 or stylometric scores.

docs.title: Dashboard Translations
docs.text:
UI translations are stored as JSON files in src/adapters/templates/i18n/:

src/adapters/templates/i18n/
├── en.json    # English (reference)
├── es.json    # Spanish
├── pt.json    # Portuguese
├── ar.json    # Arabic
└── ru.json    # Russian

The FastAPI server loads the appropriate JSON based on ?lang= and injects it into the Jinja2 template. JavaScript runtime strings use a T object:

// In the browser — T is injected by the server
document.getElementById("title").textContent = T.investigation_title;
document.getElementById("start").textContent = T.btn_start;

docs.title: PDF Reports
docs.text: PDF dossiers inherit the language from the investigation. Section headers (IDENTITY & DEMOGRAPHICS, PERFIL PSICOLÓGICO, etc.), labels, and classification tags are all rendered in the selected language.

docs.title: Contributing Translations
docs.text:
To add a new language:

  1. Copy src/adapters/templates/i18n/en.json to <code>.json
  2. Translate all values — keys must remain identical
  3. Add the language to the Language enum in src/core/domain/language.py
  4. Add the system prompt translation in src/core/services/agent_engine.py
  5. Add the option to the dashboard <select> in dashboard.html
  6. Run the consistency test:
python3 -c "
import json, glob
files = glob.glob('src/adapters/templates/i18n/*.json')
counts = {f.split('/')[-1]: len(json.load(open(f))) for f in files}
print(counts)
assert len(set(counts.values())) == 1, 'Key count mismatch!'
print('All languages consistent ✓')
"

Tip

The Spanish system prompt uses "español neutro" (neutral Spanish) — avoiding regional slang to maximize clarity for all Spanish-speaking users.

docs.title: Web Dashboard
docs.text:
The web dashboard provides a real-time visual interface for OSINT investigations, powered by WebSocket streaming from the FastAPI backend.

osint-d2 serve              # Start dashboard at http://localhost:8000
# or
docker compose up -d         # Docker deployment

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Investigation wizard with real-time agent reasoning

The dashboard is a single-page application built with vanilla JavaScript and the OSINT-D2 design system (dark intelligence theme). It communicates with the backend entirely via WebSocket.

Offline & Private

The dashboard makes zero external network requests. All JavaScript (vis-network, DOMPurify) and CSS (Font Awesome) dependencies are vendorized locally. No CDNs, no telemetry, no data leaks — suitable for air-gapped and sensitive environments.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text: Component What it shows Investigation Panel Configure target, mode, language, trust anchors, AI provider Agent Console Real-time streaming of agent reasoning steps and tool calls Social Profiles Table Discovered profiles with confirmation status, avatars, and metadata Entity Graph Interactive relationship visualization between identities AI Analysis Full 6D cognitive profile when using Agent Mode Export Actions Download JSON, PDF dossier, or HTML report

docs.title: Real-Time Architecture
docs.text:
The dashboard uses a WebSocket connection to stream investigation progress:

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant S as FastAPI Server
    participant A as Agent Engine
    participant T as OSINT Tools

    B->>S: WebSocket connect
    B->>S: Start investigation (target, mode, options)
    S->>A: Initialize agent
    loop Each reasoning step
        A->>T: Call tool (scan_username, fetch_url, etc.)
        T-->>A: Tool result
        A-->>S: Step update (tool, args, result)
        S-->>B: Stream step via WebSocket
    end
    A-->>S: Final report (6D profile)
    S-->>B: Stream complete report

Each agent step is pushed to the browser as it happens — you can watch the AI reason in real time.

docs.title: Quick Scan
docs.text: Select Username or Email mode for a fast scan across native scanners. Results appear in the social profiles table within seconds.

docs.title: Agent Mode
docs.text:
Select AI Agent for autonomous investigation:

  1. Set the AI provider (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Ollama)
  2. Set max reasoning steps (default: 10)
  3. Optionally enable breach checking
  4. Optionally add trust anchors to filter false positives
  5. Click Start Investigation

Agent reasoning steps streamed in real time

docs.title: Entity Graph
docs.text:
The dashboard renders an interactive entity graph showing relationships between discovered identities:

  • Green node — the investigation target
  • Cyan nodes — confirmed profiles (exists = YES)
  • Grey nodes — unconfirmed or non-existent profiles
  • Red markers — profiles with breach data
  • Edges — connection type (username match, email link, avatar match)

docs.title: Language Support
docs.text:
Switch languages via the sidebar dropdown or URL parameter:

http://localhost:8000/?lang=es

The dashboard UI, AI prompts, and PDF exports all adapt to the selected language. See Languages for supported languages.
